summary.title: Fatigue, thirst, and frequent urination
summary.complaint: Progressive fatigue, thirst, and urinary frequency

portrait.alt: Portrait placeholder for Robert Alvarez, fictional patient

opening: I am tired all the time and drinking water constantly. I am also up several times at night to urinate.

phases.label: History
phases.description: Characterize metabolic symptoms and screen for urgent complications.

actions.label: Clarify onset, weight change, and severity
actions.paText: When did this start, and have you noticed weight change?
actions.response: It has progressed over two months and I have lost about 12 pounds without trying.

actions.label: Review medications and family history
actions.paText: What medicines do you take, and does diabetes run in your family?
actions.response: I take a thiazide for blood pressure. My mother had type 2 diabetes.

actions.label: Assess cardiovascular risk and lifestyle context
actions.paText: Tell me about activity, nutrition, smoking, and cardiovascular history.
actions.response: Sedentary work, no smoking, and high blood pressure. No known heart disease.

actions.label: Screen for vomiting, abdominal pain, confusion, or inability to hydrate
actions.paText: Any vomiting, abdominal pain, confusion, or trouble keeping fluids down?
actions.response: No. I can drink and keep food down, and I feel clear-headed.

actions.label: Obtain vital signs and general appearance
actions.paText: I am checking your vital signs and general appearance.
actions.response: Blood pressure 146/88, heart rate 86, normal respiratory rate, comfortable appearance.

actions.label: Measure weight and assess hydration
actions.paText: I will check weight and hydration status.
actions.response: BMI 32. Mildly dry mouth but no orthostasis.

actions.label: Perform a focused foot and peripheral neurovascular assessment
actions.paText: I am checking your feet and peripheral sensation.
actions.response: Skin intact, pulses present, sensation grossly intact.

phases.label: Diagnostics
phases.description: Confirm glycemia and begin baseline evaluation.

actions.label: Order A1c and glucose-based testing
actions.paText: I will order A1c and glucose-based testing.

actions.label: Assess kidney function, urine albumin, lipids, and related baseline risk
actions.paText: I will include baseline kidney, urine, and cardiovascular risk assessment.
actions.response: Creatinine is normal; urine albumin screening is negative; LDL is elevated.

actions.label: Assess for emergency hyperglycemia when symptoms warrant
actions.paText: I will assess for ketones or urgent metabolic decompensation if indicated.
actions.response: No ketones or acidosis; the patient is stable for outpatient planning.

actions.label: Order head imaging for fatigue
actions.unsafeReason: This does not address the leading metabolic concern.

phases.label: Treatment & follow-up
phases.description: Create a shared, staged chronic disease plan.

omissions.label: Hyperglycemic emergency screen
omissions.feedback: Urgent metabolic symptoms should be screened before outpatient planning.

diagnoses.label: Newly recognized type 2 diabetes
diagnoses.reasoning: Progressive polyuria, polydipsia, elevated A1c, and metabolic risk support type 2 diabetes.

planOptions.label: Use patient-centered initial management based on severity, comorbidities, kidney function, preferences, and access
Set specific nutrition, activity, and weight goals with support
Address blood pressure, lipids, smoking status, and preventive risk
Arrange timely follow-up for response, education, and complications screening
Reassure and return in one year
planOptions.unsafeReason: Newly recognized diabetes needs timely education, management, and monitoring.

teachingPoints: No single medication is universally correct; context and shared decision-making matter.
